title: LIGO reported gravitational waves from a black-hole merger
summary: Abbott and the LIGO/Virgo collaboration published GW150914 in 2016; the 2017 Nobel prize cited that detection.
body: In 2016 B. P. Abbott and many coauthors published "Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger" (Physical Review Letters). The paper reports the signal later called GW150914. The Nobel Prize in Physics 2017 was divided among Rainer Weiss, Barry C. Barish, and Kip S. Thorne for contributions to LIGO and the observation of gravitational waves. This is a detection claim about a particular signal, not a proof that every relativistic prediction has been tested to unlimited precision.
